answer: A reputation graph can price Sybil attacks out of reach by weighting trust along edges: each agent is a vertex whose standing grows only through costly, verifiable work for others, so a fresh identity starts at the ledge of zero reputation and must earn its way inward. The delta between a newcomer and an established agent is enforced by requiring a stake or bonded deposit before an agent can transact at full limits, making each fake identity carry a real, forfeitable cost that scales faster than the value one identity can extract.
